title: Tesla reveals next generation flying Roadster sports EV with SpaceX thrusters
text:
Automaker Tesla demonstrated a redesigned roadster Thursday that can drive upside down on an inverted ramp, turn in midair and land using built-in thrusters. It also used its rockets to fly over a line of parked vehicles.
from FRI 4:00 AM CDT until SAT 1:00 AM CDT, Brazos County, Washington County, Inland Brazoria County, Chambers County, Waller County, Fort Bend County, Inland Matagorda County, Inland Galveston County, Wharton County, Inland Jackson County, Grimes County, Colorado County, Cherokee CountyThe Tesla Roadster can accelerate from 0 to 60 mph in under one second and can reach a top speed of over 230 mph, CEO Elon Musk said.
Tesla CEO Elon Musk revealed a redesigned Roadster developed in collaboration with SpaceX that features thrusters and a fan-suction system. The thrusters enable the car to fly short distances and perform rolls in mid-air while the suction system, designed to improve cornering, allowed the car to drive upside down on an inverted ramp.
Of three versions of the vehicle, the base tier requires a $50,000 deposit, the second requires a $250,000 deposit, and the top model is listed as"invite only" with no price specified.that can drive upside down on an inverted ramp, turn in midair and land using built-in thrusters. It also used its rockets to fly over a line of parked vehicles.
It was a major upgrade to the next-generation version of its electric sports car that Tesla first showed nine years ago with a plan to start production in 2028, Tesla demonstrated a redesigned roadster Thursday that can drive upside down on an inverted ramp, turn in mid-air and land using built-in thrusters. The redesigned vehicle, developed with CEO Elon Musk’s SpaceX, would accelerate from 0 to 60 mph in less than a second, which he says is "the least interesting part," given the collaboration with SpaceX.
"Advanced cold-gas thrusters use all-electric actuators to offer precise thrust, completing micro adjustments within a fraction of a second. This helps stabilize the vehicle in flight," Tesla’s website states. The vehicle uses a fan suction system on the bottom of the car that can use up to 2Gs to make the car go upside down on the inverted roadway ramp and even stick there.
"Now you might say, like, ‘How often do you want to stick upside down in a car? ’" Musk told the audience.
"Maybe not that often, but it actually has an actual benefit on the track or just driving, where the downforce of the car means you can corner incredibly well. Like you can corner like it looks like you’re breaking physics because the car sticks to the ground so hard. So acceleration cornering — it’s going to crush every track record that has ever existed.
" Of the attitude control thrusters and main thrusters, Musk said the car can "fly like a rocket" and do rolls. "It could do like crazy gymnastics, whatever you want, really," he said. "Now I should, you know, say that this is not necessarily a safety-optimized car, OK? But it takes the fun meter to 11 out of 10.
"The vehicle can also hit a top speed of over 230 mph, Musk said. Musk and his team did not reveal full prices for the vehicle during Thursday’s big reveal. Nearly a decade ago, the company quoted a base price of $200,000. The reservation page for the Roadster after the Thursday event showed a "Performance" version of the vehicle requiring a $50,000 deposit.
A "Thrust" version that features "acceleration thrusters requires a $250,000 deposit. The Source: Information in this story came from Reuters, Tesla, X and FOX Business. This story was reported from Orlando.
